name: Finish the Line, Get Featured
why_it_works: An unfinished sentence nags at the brain until someone completes it. Offering to feature the best answer turns a throwaway comment into a shot at being seen, so people write real, funny, specific answers, and the best ones become free content for the next post.

hook.pattern: Put an unfinished line on screen with a blank, and promise the best ending gets featured.
examples: {{opening_line}} ... Finish it. Best answer gets featured.
Fill in the blank. The winner goes on {{feature_prize}}.
I started the sentence. You finish it.

variables.name: brand
variables.description: Show, artist, coach or team name

variables.name: opening_line
variables.description: The open-ended sentence with a blank at the end
variables.example: The worst advice I ever got was ___

variables.name: host_example

variables.example: 'Just wing the first episode.' I did. It's still online.

variables.name: feature_prize
variables.description: How the winning answer gets featured

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 moody studio shot of an empty microphone on a boom arm, one warm practical lamp, deep shadows, haze in the light, {{brand}} sign soft in the background

beats.purpose: show your own answer to set the bar

visual.prompt: Slow push-in on the microphone in the same moody studio, lamp flickering gently, vertical 9:16
Vertical 9:16 shot of a phone on a stand showing a blurred comment, next to the studio mic, spotlight on the phone, warm haze

cta: Finish the line in the comments. The most-liked answer gets {{feature_prize}} on {{brand}}. Closes {{deadline}}.

craft.technique: Open loop with a status prize
craft.notes: Your own answer must be specific and a little self-deprecating so people feel safe to be honest. Let likes pick the winner: it doubles engagement because people come back to like their favorites.

do_not: Use a line that invites cruelty about a real person or group
Feature a commenter's answer without asking first
For musicians: drop a fan's line into a released song without a written OK
compliance: Get the commenter's permission and credit them before featuring their words on air, on screen or in a song
Musicians: if a fan's line goes into a released track, get a short written release covering credit and any songwriting share
